about.title: Brea Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Brea's mix of freeway traffic feeding into SR-57 Southbound and busy surface roads like Imperial Highway and Lambert Road creates real friction points for drivers, especially as commuter volume builds toward Friday afternoons. Public records show 211 injury collisions and 304 injured people in Orange County's most recent reporting year for this area, a reminder that even routine drives here carry risk. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories can fade quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we're a free service that connects injured Brea residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, deal with the insurance company on your behalf, and help you understand your options under California law before you say something you might regret.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity (like a city road crew) may be involved. An attorney can spot that issue early, before you lose the option to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California lets you recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. An independent attorney can push back on inflated fault percentages an insurer may try to pin on you after a Brea collision.

items.title: No Recorded Statement Without Guidance
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly, hoping for something they can use to limit your payout. You're not required to give one, and an attorney working on contingency, no fee unless you recover, can talk to the insurer for you instead.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Brea?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That timeline can shrink to as little as six months if your claim involves a government entity, such as a Caltrans-maintained stretch of SR-57. It's worth having an attorney review your situation early so you don't miss a shorter deadline.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you were partially at fault. Your total recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, so if you were found 20% responsible, you'd receive 80% of the damages awarded. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly shifted onto you.

items.question: Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can work against you. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize payouts, not protect your interests. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can communicate with insurers on your behalf, free of charge to start.
